name: רְחַבְעָם
gloss: the people is made wide; or he widens the people
summary: Rehoboam son of Solomon and Naamah the Ammonitess, king of Judah seventeen years in Jerusalem (1Ki 14:21). At Shechem he refused the elders' counsel and answered the people harshly, and ten tribes rejected the house of David, “What portion have we in David?” (1Ki 12:13–16), as Yahweh had said by Ahijah (1Ki 11:31); Shishak of Egypt came against Jerusalem in his fifth year, and he humbled himself at Shemaiah's word (2Ch 12:2–12). He is in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat 1:7, Ῥοβοάμ; the Peshitta's name is SEDRA lexeme 2991). The name is the verb רָחַב “be wide, make wide” with עָם “people”; scripture does not explain it, but under the king so named the people was not widened but divided.

evidence.note: “And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.”
Forty-one years old when he began to reign, seventeen years in Jerusalem; his mother Naamah the Ammonitess.
He answered the people harshly; Israel said, “What portion have we in David?”
Ahijah to Jeroboam: “I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon and give you ten tribes.”
Shemaiah: “You have forsaken me”; the princes and the king humbled themselves.
The verb of the name: “I will … enlarge (וְהִרְחַבְתִּי) your border.”

note: The two readings are of the form only: רְחַב‑ as a perfect with עָם as its subject (“the people is wide, has been enlarged”), or with Yahweh understood (“he widens the people”), as in Rehabiah. Not followed: Wiktionary's gloss “a people has enlarged”.
